source: Five user photographs of the Passaporte para Português glossary: pages 160, 158, 156, 154 and 152, geographical names and readable page fragments
normalization_notes: Manually transcribe pages 160, 158, 156, 154 and 152 in attachment order, including readable following-page fragments.
Page 160 continues the geographical-names section begun on page 159. Section headings and provenance remain metadata, not database categories.
Use lowercase NFC individual words; remove punctuation and trailing gender articles. Keep articles and prepositions within expressions.
Split Nova Iorque into nova and iorque while retaining the full place name and original capitalization in source JSON.
Expand teu/tua, seu/sua, ter de/que and estar com/ter sono into their components.
Separate se from vestir-se, sentar-se, sentir-se and reformar-se, preserving the full constructions as source context.
Keep lexical hyphens in terça-feira and sexta-feira. Normalize printed rés do chão to the dictionary-attested European Portuguese compound rés-do-chão, rather than treating it as a sentence.
Keep repeated noun/adjective senses and duplicate source spellings in separate source rows; import each normalized word once.
Retain the printed German glosses, including apparent errors; explain translation corrections in enrichment metadata.

dictionary_checks.note: Verified the ground-floor meaning and hyphenated European Portuguese form; the printed spaced variant is retained in extracted JSON.
Verified the standalone noun impulse/spontaneous act and the separate de repente expression suddenly.
Verified dessert; preserve the correct existing English/Ukrainian translations despite the apparent German source typo Nachttisch.

translation_notes: Nova Iorque remains a full place name in source context. Nova keeps its existing new/young translation; iorque is translated only as the York name element, not as the whole New York name.
Proper names are lowercase in SQLite, consistent with previous imports; original capitalization is retained in JSON.
Rés do chão is represented by the dictionary-attested European Portuguese lexical compound rés-do-chão, accepted by the single-word validator. No general phrase rows are introduced.
Repente is a noun, while de repente means suddenly. The phrase translation is retained in source context rather than copied onto both components.
Sobretudo follows the photographed adverb meaning above all; it is not assigned the unrelated overcoat noun sense.
Tosta means toast/toasted sandwich and mista means mixed. The ham-and-cheese meaning belongs to the full tosta mista expression.
Semiequipado follows the source partially equipped meaning without assuming that it necessarily means furnished.
Reformar includes the pronominal retire meaning with se, while the attached pronoun is stored separately.
Significa is the verb form means/signifies, not the entire O que significa? question.
The photographed German column contains Nachttisch for sobremesa and English return for regressar. Original glosses are kept unchanged, and translations follow Portuguese meanings.
Existing receita and tocar already cover both photographed senses. Existing senha, ténis, vestido and tempo have additional meanings recorded for review.
New entries start at mastery 0. Existing IDs, translations, levels and practice history are preserved.
